stem: The news has been brought to us by him. (Change to Simple sentence)
options: He has brought us the news.
He brought the news to us.
We brought the news to him.
rationale: Transforms sentence structure as directed preserving semantic meaning.

stem: They created such a fuss over a trivial matter. (Change to Simple sentence)
options: Such a fuss is being created over a trivial matter.
Such a fuss was created over a trivial matter.
Such a fuss has been created over a trivial matter.
By then such a fuss has been created over a trivial matter.
rationale: Transforms sentence structure without alteration of meaning.

stem: Although he was wealthy and educated, he never made a name. (Change to Simple sentence)
options: He was wealthy and educated, but never made a name.
Inspite of being wealthy and educated, he never made a name.
He never made a name because he was wealthy and educated.
Since he was wealthy and educated, he never made a name.
rationale: Transforms sentence structure according to grammatical specification.

stem: It is kind of you to visit us. (Change to Exclamatory sentence)
options: How kind of you to visit us!
How kind it is of you to visit us!
It is so kind you visit us!
How kind of you that you visit us!
rationale: Transforms sentence structure preserving proposition.

stem: O that I could fly like birds! (Change to Assertive sentence)
options: How I wish I could fly like birds.
I wish that I could fly like birds.
I wish to fly like birds.
How I wish to fly like birds.
rationale: Transforms sentence as directed.

stem: If you speak the truth, you will be honoured. (Change to Compound sentence)
options: Speak the truth and you will be honoured.
Speak the truth to be honoured.
Speaking the truth will honour you.
Speak the truth so that you would be honoured.
rationale: Transforms sentence structure as directed.

stem: He worked hard to earn money. (Change to Complex sentence)
options: He worked hard as to earn money.
He worked hard and earn money.
He worked hard that he might earn money.
He worked hard so he could earn money.
rationale: Transforms simple sentence into complex sentence with purpose clause 'that he might earn money'.

stem: He is better than any other student. (Change to Superlative degree)
options: He is best than other studens.
He is best of the students.
He is best student of all.
rationale: Transforms comparative degree into superlative degree 'He is the best student'.

stem: The patient is so weak that he cannot move about. (Change to Simple sentence)
options: The patient is too weak and cannot move about.
The patient is too weak to move about.
The patient cannot move about as he is too weak.
Because the patient is too weak, he cannot move about.
rationale: Transforms complex sentence with result clause into simple sentence with 'too weak to move about'.

stem: No other boy in the class is as tall as John. (Use Comparative degree)
options: John is the tallest boy in class.
John is taller of all the boys in the class.
John is taller than any other boy in the class.
John is taller than many boys in the class.
rationale: Transforms positive degree into comparative degree 'John is taller than any other boy in the class'.

stem: The dinner was over. The guests were shown out. They got into their cars.
options: The dinner was over and the guests got into their cars as they were shown out.
The dinner having been over, the guests were shown out to get into their cars.
As the dinner was over, the guests were shown out and got into their cars.
The dinner getting over, the guests were shown out and they got into their cars.
rationale: Synthesises three clauses into single sentence using participial absolute phrase.

stem: It is very hot. One cannot go out.
options: It is too hot to go out.
It is very hot and one cannot go out.
One cannot go out as it is very hot.
It is too hot and one cannot go out.
rationale: Synthesises clauses into single periodic sentence.

stem: She stood on tip-toe. She reached for the mangoes on the tree.
options: She reached for the mangoes on the tree by standing tip-toed.
She reached for the mangoes on tree when she stood on tip-toe.
Standing on tip-toe she reached for the mangoes on the tree.
She reached the mangoes on the tree standing on tip-toe.
rationale: Synthesises sentences into single compound or complex structure.

stem: I must finish this novel. There are still few chapters.
options: I still have few chapters in the novel to finish.
I still have few chapters in the novel before I finish.
Few chapters are still left for me to finish the novel.
There a still few chapters for me to finish the novel.
rationale: Synthesises sentences into coherent single sentence.

stem: They decided to start a travel group. All agreed to this.
options: They all agreed to start a travel group.
They jointly decided to start a travel group.
They agreed to jointly start a travel group.
They unanimously decided to start a travel group.
rationale: Synthesises sentences into single complex sentence using relative clause.

stem: Ani speaks English. She also speaks French.
options: Ani speaks English as well as French.
Ani speaks English apart from French.
Ani speaks both English and French.
rationale: Synthesises sentences using conjunctions or participial structures.

stem: Get inside. You may catch cold.
options: Get inside else you may catch cold.
You may catch cold, get inside.
Get inside, otherwise you may catch cold.
Get inside or you may catch cold.
rationale: Synthesises alternatives into single sentence using alternative coordinator 'or / otherwise'.

stem: She was honest. This was his statement. It was right.
options: He rightly said in his statement that she was honest.
She was rightly said as honest in his statement.
His statement was right in which he said she was honest.
His statement that she was honest was right.
rationale: Synthesises three propositions into single sentence with noun clause in apposition 'His statement that she was honest was right'.

stem: Mohan is industrious. He is very particular in his work.
options: Mohan is very particular in his work as he is industrious.
Mohan is not only industrious but also very particular in his work.
Mohan is industrious and particular in his work.
Mohan is industrious as well as particular in his work.
rationale: Synthesises sentences using correlative conjunction 'not only... but also'.

stem: James is my friend. He is the son of a doctor.
options: James is my friend and is the son of a doctor.
James who is my friend is also the son of a doctor.
James, my friend, is the son of a doctor.
James, my friend, who is the son of a doctor.
rationale: Synthesises sentences using noun phrase in apposition 'James, my friend, is the son of a doctor'.
